_note: SCHEMA ONLY, EMPTY ROSTER. The measured section library is BRAND data: it is generated from the brand's built web masters (asset-production builds them; measure each slot at each breakpoint) and named in the pack's `section_library` role. page_lint.js reads that file, or --sections; this file is what it falls back to, and it refuses to grade a page against an empty roster. Never populate this file with one brand's geometry: grading a page against another brand's geometry is worse than not grading it.

_schema.sections: array of section objects: {id: 'W01', name, reach, breakpoints: [names from `breakpoints`], slots: {<slot>: {budget: {<breakpoint>: chars}, role, note}}, requires_verbatim, seo_block, open_decision, note}. A slot that is NOT RENDERED at a breakpoint carries budget 0 there, never an omitted key: copy written into it disappears rather than truncating.
_schema.page_types: map of page type id to {label, typical: [section ids], requires: [section ids]}
_schema.breakpoints: map of breakpoint name to {label, width, note}; the names are what pages declare
_schema.pins: {slotmap_generated, checked_on}: which slotmap_web the budgets were measured against

pins.note: Null in the engine. The pack's section library carries real pins.

_budget_method.how: chars ≈ (slot width in px ÷ (font size × 0.52)) × lines. 0.52 is the average advance ratio for the brand's type stacks at these sizes; it is a planning figure, not a renderer.
_budget_method.why: A slot budget is not a style preference. These components are built to measured site geometry — a card title that overruns re-wraps and changes the card's height, and on a fixed-height mobile slide it clips. The budget is the shape of the box the copy has to live in.
_budget_method.confidence: Budgets are DERIVED, not measured per string. They are a warning threshold, not a ceiling: over budget means look at it in the file, not that it is wrong.
